newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-FEHR KEEPS TWO-SHOT LEAD IN LAS VEGAS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-FEHR KEEPS TWO-SHOT LEAD IN LAS VEGAS.

text.p: Rick Fehr was not nearly as
spectacular Friday as he was Thursday, but he was good enough
for a 3-under par 69 to keep a two-shot lead after 54 holes of
the 90-hole Las Vegas Invitational golf tournament.
Davis Love III and Fred Funk are two shots off the pace in
this tournament played over three courses.
Fehr, who had a 10-under 62 in Thursday's second round,
birdied three of his first four holes Friday but then had to
take a double bogey 7 on the ninth hole that slowed him down.
"I played fairly solid, but I hit a few bad shots and they
ended up costing me," said Fehr, who played the back nine at
2-under. "This course isn't easy, so to have a double bogey
and still shoot 3-under is good."
Fehr, though, had little breathing room as the players
continued their assault on par at the three courses.
Love shot an 8-under 64 at TPC Summerlin to drop to
18-under, while Funk had an up-and-down 68 to tie Love for
second at 18-under.
Funk, who did not have a bogey in the first two rounds,
birdied the first four holes at the Desert Inn to go from
14-under to 18-under. But he found some trouble threw the
middle of the course and took a disheartening bogey at 18 that
dropped him into a tie for second.
He three-putted from 15 feet because he was looking into
an extremely bright sun that he said temporarily blinded him.
"The sun was really tough there," Funk said. "It was
coming right over the top of the Desert Inn Hotel and that
made it very tough for me."
Fehr went off in the first group of the day at 6:50 a.m.
He said he did his best work before the sun was completely up.
"I played pretty well before 8 o'clock," Fehr said. "But
it got breezy and I didn't get it close later in the round."
